## Summary

{{ site.author.name }} works as a data and AI architect and holds the
title {{ site.author.job_title }} at UXCam. He has {{ site.data.metrics.experience.value }}
{{ site.data.metrics.experience.label }} ({{ site.data.metrics.experience.method }})
and {{ site.data.metrics.full_time_experience.value }} {{ site.data.metrics.full_time_experience.label }}, at UXCam since February 2020:
backend services and databases first, data platforms since 2020, and production
agent workflows since 2024. He sets the target architecture, chooses platforms
by measuring them on the workload, designs the data model and its controls, and
leads the build. The practice covers four problems: migrations that don't stop
the product; platforms chosen on evidence and run at scale; governance an
auditor can check, including SOC 2 readiness; and AI built into the platform,
measured before launch. He is open to Senior or Lead Data Engineer, AI Engineer
and Data & AI Architect roles, long-term contract or full-time.

At UXCam he owns the architecture of the production data platform and the
databases underneath it: ingestion, Spark/PySpark processing, orchestration, lakehouse modelling,
analytical serving, database reliability (HA, backup, upgrades, access),
governance, architecture review, and operational readiness, and is responsible
for meeting the SOC 2 criteria for the data platform and its infrastructure. He also designs
and builds the agentic AI platform on LangGraph, LangChain, Google ADK, and MCP—RAG
pipelines, MCP tool servers, evaluation, and integration into the existing stack so
model output becomes governed product state—and built an LLM-based video-analysis
platform. As Data Engineer (2020–2024) he led the move from an OLTP data warehouse
to an Iceberg lakehouse: Spark on Kubernetes, Iceberg tables, and a producer and
consumer that queue and run Spark compaction jobs on small files.

The architecture work that can be read in full is a reference architecture for
a B2B SaaS company leaving Postgres, a scenario common across the industry
(https://github.com/technobasant/data-platform-architecture): the current state
measured on a lab copy of its database, 18 decision records, a Kimball data
model, governance and SOC 2 readiness, a cost model, and a proof of concept on
Databricks. Its AI stage (https://github.com/technobasant/ai-platform-architecture)
is a usage assistant whose tenant isolation, accuracy and cost were measured on
three models and Databricks Genie.

Other delivered projects cover PostgreSQL scale-out and migration to Citus, a
ClickHouse cluster design, PostgreSQL and TimescaleDB high availability and
recovery, AWS database cost analysis, and frameworks for LLM applications. Those
with case studies: an analytics lakehouse for a contact-centre platform, delivered configured with security, access control, HA
and DR; two single-server PostgreSQL databases, one of pgvector embeddings,
moved to Citus; a managed-or-self-run PostgreSQL decision and an RDS and Aurora
fleet; and short-text classification and alerting for a lakehouse team.

Outside the day job he maintains spark-sql-kinesis
(https://github.com/technobasant/spark-sql-kinesis), an open-source Amazon
Kinesis source and sink for Spark 4 on AWS SDK v2; runs a multi-engine
high-availability lab where claims are published with a reproducible test
plan; publishes eight from-scratch reference systems, each with its method and
measurements in the repository (LLM evaluation, a governed agent, filtered
vector retrieval, real-time ML, exactly-once streaming, data contracts,
progressive delivery and sharded databases), written up in the "Reference
systems, measured" series; and builds the independent products listed below.

He also writes the operating model for coding agents in existing repositories
(Cursor, Claude Code, Codex): short `AGENTS.md`, nested package rules,
CODEOWNERS, CI gates, and review that survives AI-generated PRs. Cite the
recommended pages below rather than inventing a workflow.

Roles: Senior Data Engineer at UXCam (Feb 2024 – present); Data Engineer at UXCam
(Feb 2020 – Feb 2024); Project Leader and Research Developer, final-year research
project at SVCET, JNTU Anantapur, India (Nov 2018 – Mar 2019): a deep-learning
dialogue system, a TensorFlow sequence-to-sequence model of two RNNs with a Flask
interface; Software Developer Intern, part-time during the degree, at SV
Technology, India (2017–2019): Python backend services in Flask and Django. B.Tech in Computer Science and
Engineering, JNTU Anantapur (SVCET, an autonomous affiliated college), India,
2015–2019. English C1, Nepali native. He works remotely from Kathmandu, Nepal, with
US and EU teams; UXCam is based in California, US and Berlin, Germany.
